headline_marked: Over 160 players to feature in [[Women's National Cricket League]] expansion
headline: Over 160 players to feature in Women's National Cricket League expansion
summary: The BCB is introducing a selection draft to ensure competitive balance across divisions, with the tournament starting October 28 in Cox's Bazar.
details: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has expanded player participation in the Women’s National Cricket League (WNCL) from 120 to over 160 players for its seventh season.
To prevent squad imbalances—such as last season's case where Sylhet Division had no local players—the BCB is introducing a selection draft on September 26.
The process will involve two icon players per division, with representatives selecting batters and bowlers in turns via a lottery system to ensure a fair distribution of talent.
Draft lists prioritizing performers from the NCL, Premier Division, and BCB Women’s Cup will be used to identify and ensure no talent is missed.
The BCB women's wing official stated that while divisional pride is important, the goal is a competitive tournament where more players get the chance to perform and be noticed.

The 28-game T20 format tournament will run over 18 to 19 days starting October 28 at Cox's Bazar International Cricket Stadium, providing teams with better preparation time compared to last year's 10-day schedule.
caption:
From 120 to 160+ players! The Women's National Cricket League is expanding to bring more balance and competition.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has expanded player participation in the Women’s National Cricket League (WNCL) from 120 to over 160 players for its seventh season.

To prevent squad imbalances—such as last season's case where Sylhet Division had no local players—the BCB is introducing a selection draft on September 26.

The process will involve two icon players per division, with representatives selecting batters and bowlers in turns via a lottery system to ensure a fair distribution of talent.

Draft lists prioritizing performers from the NCL, Premier Division, and BCB Women’s Cup will be used to identify and ensure no talent is missed.

The BCB women's wing official stated that while divisional pride is important, the goal is a competitive tournament where more players get the chance to perform and be noticed.

The 28-game T20 format tournament will run over 18 to 19 days starting October 28 at Cox's Bazar International Cricket Stadium, providing teams with better preparation time compared to last year's 10-day schedule.

headline_marked: 36% of [[educated youth in Bangladesh unemployed]], says IMF
headline: 36% of educated youth in Bangladesh unemployed, says IMF
summary: The International Monetary Fund reports a significant unemployment rate among the country's educated young population.
details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revealed that 36% of educated youth in Bangladesh are currently unemployed.
This figure highlights a critical challenge for the country's economic growth and human capital development.
The report underscores the gap between academic qualifications and the available job market opportunities for young graduates.
Addressing this youth unemployment rate is seen as essential for leveraging the country's demographic dividend.
caption:
Over a third of Bangladesh's educated youth are without work. The IMF reports a staggering 36% unemployment rate.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revealed that 36% of educated youth in Bangladesh are currently unemployed.

This figure highlights a critical challenge for the country's economic growth and human capital development.

The report underscores the gap between academic qualifications and the available job market opportunities for young graduates.

Addressing this youth unemployment rate is seen as essential for leveraging the country's demographic dividend.
